correctness.rationale: On rank-two 2×n matrices representing Gr(2,n), the equations det(v_i,v_{i+1})=0 force nonzero columns into proportional consecutive blocks. For exact zero set Z with r nonempty blocks, the relative Gr(2,r) bundle over block lines gives dimension n−|Z|+r−4. For n>=4, r>=2 and r<=|Z|+1, with equality exactly for nonempty independent interior Z; these strata have dimension n−3, giving Fib_n−1 distinct top-dimensional irreducible closures. The n−1 hyperplanes have their expected codimension on the smooth Gr(2,n); regular sequence implies lci/CM. At generic top-dimensional strata the displayed differential criterion has full rank, giving generic reducedness and hence reducedness by CM S1+R0. Adjunction yields ω=O(−1); the Grassmann Plücker degree is Catalan_{n−2}. For df_i=det(dv_i,v_{i+1})+det(v_i,dv_{i+1}), consecutive zero columns make an equation's differential vanish; with isolated zero columns all nonzero-run edge rows eliminate independently, and each interior zero contributes two independent linear constraints exactly when det(v_{j−1},v_{j+1})≠0; endpoint zeros contribute one rank. Thus the boxed pointwise smoothness test holds in every characteristic. A specified generic pair of consecutive interior zeros with independent left/right block directions reduces to ab=0 after gauge and regular coordinates: a two-branch transverse node. Fresh independent row-space enumeration (not saved source checker) and Jacobian calculations for all Gr(2,n)(F_q) with q=2, n=4..7 and q=3,n=4..5 reproduced smooth-point tests and Fibonacci component indices. The all-characteristic argument is geometric, not an extrapolation from those finite fields.
